q: Show me how life expectancy changed in India, China and Brazil since 1990.
answer:
**Life expectancy at birth increased in all three countries since 1990:**

| Country | 1990 | 2023 | Change |
|---------|------|------|--------|
| India (IN) | 58.6 years | 72.0 years | +13.4 years |
| China (CN) | 68.2 years | 78.0 years | +9.8 years |
| Brazil (BR) | 65.9 years | 75.9 years | +10.0 years |

India saw the largest improvement (+13.4 years), while China and Brazil gained roughly 10 years each. The chart above shows the full time series from 1990 to 2023.

**Source:** World Bank indicator SP.DYN.LE00.IN (Life expectancy at birth, total, years) for India, China, and Brazil, 1990–2023. Data may be subject to a 1–2 year publication lag.
insight: All three countries saw steady improvements since 1990. India gained the most (+13.4 years), while China and Brazil both rose by about 10 years. Note: The World Bank data may have a lag of one to two years, so the latest full year might be 2023 or 2022.

q: How did youth unemployment in Spain, Italy and Greece evolve after the 2008 crisis?
answer:
Youth unemployment in Spain, Italy and Greece experienced a dramatic increase following the 2008 crisis, with all three countries peaking between 2013-2014 before gradually recovering.

**Key evolution:**

| Country | 2008 | Peak Year & Value | 2023 | Change from peak |
|---------|------|-------------------|------|------------------|
| Spain | 24.45% | 2013: **55.48%** | 28.67% | -26.8 pp |
| Italy | 21.20% | 2014: **42.68%** | 22.73% | -20.9 pp |
| Greece | 21.76% | 2013: **58.66%** | 26.62% | -32.0 pp |

**Summary:**
- **Impact was most severe in Greece**, which saw the largest spike (+37 percentage points from 2008) and remained highest throughout the period.
- All three countries reached their peak around 2013-2014 as austerity measures and economic turmoil hit hardest during this period.
- Recovery has been gradual: by 2023, all three countries had recovered significantly from their peaks, though Greece and Spain still remain above their 2008 levels, while Italy nearly returned to pre-crisis figures.

**Source:** World Bank indicator `SL.UEM.1524.NE.ZS` (Unemployment, youth total (% of total labor force ages 15-24)) for Spain (ES), Italy (IT), Greece (GR), 2008-2023.
insight: All three countries saw youth unemployment spike after 2008 (peaking around 2013-2014: Greece 58.7%, Spain 55.5%, Italy 42.7%). Since then, all have improved but remain above 2008 levels (Spain 28.7%, Italy 22.7%, Greece 26.6% in 2023).

q: Fit a linear trend to Kenya's GDP growth from 2000 to 2023. What is the slope per year and is it significant?
answer:
The linear trend in Kenya's GDP growth from 2000 to 2023 has a slope of **0.08% per year**, but it is **not statistically significant** (p = 0.21).

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Slope (change per year) | +0.08% |
| T-statistic | 1.29 |
| P-value | 0.21 |
| 95% CI for slope | [-0.05%, +0.22%] |
| Significant? | No (p > 0.05) |

The confidence interval includes zero, meaning the upward trend is not distinguishable from random variation. GDP growth has been quite volatile year-to-year, which reduces the statistical power to detect a smooth linear trend.

**Source:** World Bank indicator NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG (GDP growth, annual %), Kenya (KE), years 2000–2023.

q: Which country had the biggest drop in CO2 emissions per capita between 2000 and 2022: UK, France, Germany, USA or Japan?
answer:
**Answer: The United States had the largest drop in CO₂ emissions per capita between 2000 and 2022, decreasing by about 6.6 t CO₂e/capita.**

| Country | 2000 value (t CO₂e/cap) | 2022 value (t CO₂e/cap) | Drop (t CO₂e/cap) |
|---------|------------------------:|------------------------:|------------------:|
| USA | 21.0 | 14.4 | **6.6** |
| UK | 9.4 | 4.8 | 4.6 |
| Germany | 10.6 | 7.9 | 2.7 |
| France | 6.6 | 4.5 | 2.1 |
| Japan | 9.8 | 8.4 | 1.4 |

*Note: The World Bank publishes with a lag of one to two years, so the latest available year for this indicator is 2022.*

**Source:** World Bank indicator `EN.GHG.CO2.PC.CE.AR5` (Carbon dioxide emissions excluding LULUCF per capita), United Kingdom (GB), France (FR), Germany (DE), USA (US), Japan (JP), 2000–2022.

q: Compare government spending on education (% of GDP) in Finland, Estonia and Poland over the last decade as a bar chart.
answer:
The bar chart above compares government spending on education as a percentage of GDP for **Finland**, **Estonia** and **Poland** in 2015 and 2022.

Key takeaways:
- **Finland** consistently spends the most, starting at **7.07% in 2015** and declining to **6.38% in 2022**.
- **Estonia** stays in a stable middle range: **5.05% → 5.21%**.
- **Poland** spends the least and also shows a downward trend: **4.79% → 4.31%**.

The data is from World Bank indicator **SE.XPD.TOTL.GD.ZS** (Government expenditure on education, total (% of GDP)), published with a typical lag of 1–2 years; the latest available year is 2022.
insight: Finland consistently spends the most on education (7.07% in 2015, 6.38% in 2022). Estonia is intermediate (5.05%, 5.21%) and Poland the least (4.79%, 4.31%). All three saw declines from 2015 to 2022.

q: Яка частка відновлюваної енергії в Україні та Польщі за останні 10 років? Хто має кращу динаміку?
answer:
**Відсоток відновлюваної енергії:**

| Країна | Початок періоду (2015) | Кінець періоду (2021)* | Зміна (абс.) | Відносний ріст |
|--------|-------------------------|------------------------|--------------|----------------|
| **Україна** | 4.2% | 8.9% | **+4.7 п.п.** | **+111.9%** |
| **Польща** | 11.9% | 15.2% | **+3.3 п.п.** | **+27.7%** |

*З 2022 року дані відсутні (відбулася війна в Україні). Даних за 2022-2024 роки немає, тому взяті до 2021 року.

**Хто має кращу динаміку?**
- **Україна**: більше зросла відносно початкового рівня (+112%), хоча залишається далеким від абсолютних показників Польщі.
- **Польща**: вищий абсолютний рівень (з 13.8% у середньому проти 6.9%) і більш повільний відносний ріст.

**Висновок:** Україна демонструє кращу динаміку розвитку відновлюваної енергетики відносно початкового рівня, досягнувши майже вдвічі більшої частки за останні 7 років, при цьому Польща має значно вищий абсолютний рівень використання відновлюваних джерел енергії.
